messages.author: a1ad2f53c2c0f4dc
messages.subject: se is NA (loo output)
parts:
I am trying to compare two non-linear models of hyperbolic-discounting that I fit with brms.  The basic question is to test whether different treatments cause subjects to behave differently (as in the full model) or whether there is just a population scaling effect (e.g. the whole population shifts between treatments) but individual subjects use essentially the same strategy in different treatments.

"Full" Model:


full_model = bf(choice ~ inv_logit((rewmag/(1 + exp(logk)*delay) - smag)/noise),
                  noise ~ (1|subjid), logk ~ (treat|subjid), nl = TRUE)


full_fit = brm(full_model,
             data = all_trials, family = bernoulli(link='identity'),
             prior = c(prior(normal(-3,4), nlpar = 'logk'), prior(normal(1,10),lb = 0, nlpar = 'noise')),
             inits = "0",
             chains = 10, iter = 10000, warmup=2000, cores = 10)




"Simpler" Model


simple_model = bf(choice ~ inv_logit((rewmag/(1 + exp(logk)*delay) - smag)/noise),
 noise ~ (1|subjid), logk ~ (1|treat) + (1|subjid), nl = TRUE)


simple_fit = brm(simple_model,
 data = all_trials, family = bernoulli(link='identity'),
 prior = c(prior(normal(-3,4), nlpar = 'logk'), prior(normal(1,10),lb = 0, nlpar = 'noise')),
 inits = "0",
 chains = 20, iter = 25000, warmup=10000, cores = 22)


Both models ran with OK diagnostics (reasonable number of effective samples, Rhat ~ 1).

However, when I run `loo` to do model comparison I get this:


> loo::loo(extract_log_lik(simple_fit$fit, parameter_name = 'lp__')) . # is the lp__ the right thing to use here?
Computed from 200000 by 1 log-likelihood matrix

          Estimate SE
elpd_loo -13748.1 NA
p_loo        91.9 NA
looic     27496.3 NA

Pareto k diagnostic values:
 Count Pct 
(-Inf, 0.5] (good) 0 0.0%
 (0.5, 0.7] (ok) 0 0.0%
 (0.7, 1] (bad) 0 0.0%
 (1, Inf) (very bad) 1 100.0%
See help('pareto-k-diagnostic') for details.
Warning message:
Some Pareto k diagnostic values are too high. See help('pareto-k-diagnostic') for details. 

Why is the SE==NA?
What does it mean that the Pareto k diagnostic values are too bad. How can I compare the models?

I tried to read Vehtari, et al (2016) but it is over my head.  (Apologies if this would be better asked in a different group).
